pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

4. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. blue

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

8. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.

10. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: Simple prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Composition – self assessment 9.5.1 Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Sho and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

3. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

5. C — run

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

7. C — went

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

11. B — Where is the library?

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: Simple prepositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition – self assessment 9.5.1 Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Sho; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
